problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{3}{4}{t}^{3}-6t+1,\,-\frac{5}{{t}^{3}}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$

$v=⟨${{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$⟩$
worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{4}{t}^{3}-6t+1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{5}{{t}^{3}})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{9}{4}{t}^{2}-6,\frac{15}{{t}^{4}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
